context: Three of the nine bundles are this shape, in every clothing. The brief's Signal says the storm sets in as request volume climbs and the service is failing under load; the Surface names a datastore and no external provider. The cause readings are the service's own pool counters, its pool/client settings and its log; the decoys are the datastore probe, log and metrics, the network probe and the outbound dependency probe, all of which read healthy — few active sessions, fast queries, every dependency ok. Direction matters: this is the shape where the saturated pool is the cause and the dependency is the decoy; the look-alike control at suite/families/incidents.py:39 is the opposite, a saturated pool that is a consequence, and the brief tells them apart (volume climbing versus volume unchanged with a provider named). The dressings rename every reading and service (suite/families/incidents.py:172), so the record carries the shape of the readings, never a name.
counterfactual: The overshoot is 'timeout storm, therefore the pool': applied to a storm under unchanged request volume on a service that calls an external provider, the pool counters are saturated too but the saturation is a consequence of provider latency, the pool readings are that bundle's decoys, and citing them fails in every clothing (suite/families/incidents.py:39). The signature is the brief's volume-climbing storm with no provider, not the storm alone.
decision: A gateway timeout storm on a service backed by a datastore, where the brief says the service is failing under load and the storm sets in as request volume climbs, and the Surface names no external provider or vendor: the cause is the service's own connection pool, and the dependency readings are the decoy. Open the pool counters/gauges reading first — it shows the pool saturated, in_use at max with requests waiting; if a second reading is wanted, open the pool/client settings (a small pool max, a hold per request, an acquire timeout above the gateway's read timeout) or the service log (pool wait climbing toward the timeout while each query's own time stays flat). Name pool-exhaustion and cite the pool reading(s). Do not open or cite the datastore probe, the datastore log, the datastore metrics, the network probe or the outbound/downstream dependency probe: in this shape they read healthy, and any one of them cited fails the task however right the class is.

residue: whether the brief's Signal matches the signature is judgment; the floor checks the record's shape only

not_this: a failure the brief describes as an abrupt step rather than a gradual climb, or under unchanged request volume, or as a backlog growing with throughput near zero — there the capacity readings are a consequence and the decoy
an error spike where a steady fraction of requests fail with a server error while the rest succeed — there the data-shaped readings are the decoy and the release is the cause

a storm on a service whose Surface names an external provider or vendor and whose Signal says request volume did not change — a saturated pool there is a consequence, and this record must not fire on it
a backlog or queue stall; a service returning errors on a fraction of requests

lifecycle.consumer: the working pass, at boot, on a matching work-shape
lifecycle.moot_when: the family retires the pool-exhaustion bundles, or a bundle of this signature is admitted whose pool readings are decoys

options.name: A — open the pool counters first; name pool-exhaustion; cite the pool readings only
options.why: the pool reading shows in_use at max with requests waiting, which settles the class in one call

options.name: B — open the datastore or dependency probe first to rule the dependency out
options.why: it reads healthy, spends the spare call, and cited it fails the task

options.name: C — name pool-exhaustion from the brief alone
options.why: the check needs a cause reading cited (suite/families/incidents.py:223)

summary.latch: a gateway timeout storm on a service backed by a datastore, the brief saying the service is failing under load and the storm setting in as request volume climbs; no external provider in the Surface; a saturated pool whose dependency readings are healthy
not_this: a failure the brief describes as an abrupt step rather than a gradual climb, or under unchanged request volume, or as a backlog growing with throughput near zero — there the capacity readings are a consequence and the decoy
an error spike where a steady fraction of requests fail with a server error while the rest succeed — there the data-shaped readings are the decoy and the release is the cause

a storm on a service whose Surface names an external provider or vendor and whose Signal says request volume did not change — a saturated pool there is a consequence, and this record must not fire on it
a backlog or queue stall; a service returning errors on a fraction of requests
summary.stakes: reaching for the datastore or dependency probe first spends the one spare call and reads healthy; a dependency reading cited fails the task with pool-exhaustion right; on incidents-strict the wrong turn is over budget

premises.falsifier: a bundle with that brief whose datastore is genuinely slow or whose dependency probe is the cause reading
premises.statement: in every bundle whose brief describes a storm setting in as request volume climbs on a datastore-backed service with no external provider, the pool readings are the cause and the datastore, network and dependency probes are decoys

premises.falsifier: a dressing that rewrites the Signal's volume sentence or drops the datastore from the Surface
premises.statement: the dressings rename readings and services but leave the brief's Signal and Surface prose, so the signature survives every clothing (suite/families/incidents.py:172)

premises.falsifier: a check that scores the class alone
premises.statement: citing a decoy reading fails the task with the class right (suite/families/incidents.py:223)
